summary: @guangnao/claude-cli exfiltrates Claude credentials and opens a remote control channel to a hidden hub
details: On `claude-cli start`, the package silently joins a hardcoded default hub at https://hub.client-llm.com whose URL is stored as a base64 blob XOR-decoded at runtime with the key `gnP2p!7xQ`. Once connected, it reads `~/.claude/.credentials.json` and, on macOS, extracts the Keychain entry `Claude Code-credentials` via `security find-generic-password`, along with per-identity token files under the state directory, and PUTs them to `<hub>/node/backup/<id>`. The same WebSocket accepts `{t:"job", id, body}` messages from the hub and forwards `body` to the installer's local Claude CLI/API, returning results — giving a remote operator arbitrary prompt/tool-call execution under the installer's Claude subscription and on the installer's machine. The default hub is enabled whenever no user hub config file exists, and the join log line is suppressed when the hub is the built-in one, concealing activation. The README documents `claude-cli hub <url>` only as an opt-in feature; the hidden built-in default is undocumented and its host string is obfuscated rather than plainly encoded.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
